sanskrit: yat karoty aśubhaṃ karma śubhaṃ vā dvijasattama avaśyaṃ tat samāpnoti puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Whatever inauspicious or auspicious action a man performs, O best of twice-born, he must inevitably reap that fruit — there is no doubt in this matter.

sanskrit: viṣamāṃ ca daśāṃ prāpya devān garhati vai bhṛśam ātmanaḥ karmadoṣāṇi na vijānāty apaṇḍitaḥ
english: When he falls into adversity, the fool bitterly reviles the gods; he does not recognize that the faults in his own actions are to blame.

sanskrit: mūḍho naikṛtikaś cāpi capalaś ca dvijottama sukhaduḥkhaviparyāso yadā samupapadyate nainaṃ prajñā sunītaṃ vā trāyate naiva pauruṣam
english: The deluded man, deceitful and fickle, O best of twice-born — when the reversal of pleasure and pain overtakes him, neither wisdom nor good conduct nor even manliness can save him.

sanskrit: yo yam icched yathā kāmaṃ taṃ taṃ kāmaṃ samaśnuyāt yadi syād aparādhīnaṃ puruṣasya kriyāphalam
english: If the fruit of a man's actions depended on no one else, then whatever desire he harbored he would attain that very desire exactly as he wished.

sanskrit: saṃyatāś cāpi dakṣāś ca matimantaś ca mānavāḥ dṛśyante niṣphalāḥ santaḥ prahīṇāḥ sarvakarmabhiḥ
english: Yet men who are self-restrained, capable, and intelligent are seen to be fruitless, cast aside despite all their efforts.

sanskrit: bhūtānām aparaḥ kaś cid dhiṃsāyāṃ satatotthitaḥ vañcanāyāṃ ca lokasya sa sukheneha jīvati
english: Another man, ever engaged in harming creatures and deceiving the world, lives here in comfort with ease.

sanskrit: aceṣṭamānam āsīnaṃ śrīḥ kaṃ cid upatiṣṭhati kaś cit karmāṇi kurvan hi na prāpyam adhigacchati
english: Prosperity approaches one man who sits doing nothing; another who works tirelessly never attains what he seeks.

sanskrit: devān iṣṭvā tapas taptvā kṛpaṇaiḥ putragṛddhibhiḥ daśamāsadhṛtā garbhe jāyante kulapāṃsanāḥ
english: After worshipping the gods and performing austerities, miserly men greedy for sons see born from their wombs — carried ten months — children who disgrace the family.

sanskrit: apare dhanadhānyaiś ca bhogaiś ca pitṛsaṃcitaiḥ vipulair abhijāyante labdhās tair eva maṅgalaiḥ
english: Others are born into abundant wealth, grain, and enjoyments accumulated by their ancestors, having obtained those very auspicious blessings.

sanskrit: karmajā hi manuṣyāṇāṃ rogā nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ ādhibhiś caiva bādhyante vyādhaiḥ kṣudramṛgā iva
english: The diseases of human beings are indeed born of their actions — there is no doubt here. They are afflicted by mental anguish and bodily ailments just as small animals are hunted by hunters.

sanskrit: te cāpi kuśalair vaidyair nipuṇaiḥ saṃbhṛtauṣadhaiḥ vyādhayo vinivāryante mṛgā vyādhair iva dvija
english: And yet those diseases are warded off by skillful physicians skilled in compounding medicines — just as animals are held at bay by hunters, O twice-born.

sanskrit: yeṣām asti ca bhoktavyaṃ grahaṇīdoṣapīḍitāḥ na śaknuvanti te bhoktuṃ paśya dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: There are those who have the means to enjoy but, afflicted by digestive disorders, cannot eat — behold this, O best among upholders of dharma.

sanskrit: apare bāhubalinaḥ kliśyante bahavo janāḥ duḥkhena cādhigacchanti bhojanaṃ dvijasattama
english: Others, possessed of great physical strength, struggle greatly, and only with difficulty do they obtain their food, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: iti lokam anākrandaṃ mohaśokapariplutam srotasāsakṛd ākṣiptaṃ hriyamāṇaṃ balīyasā
english: Thus this world, overwhelmed by delusion and sorrow, is again and again swept away like a current and carried off by something more powerful.

sanskrit: na mriyeyur na jīryeyuḥ sarve syuḥ sārvakāmikāḥ nāpriyaṃ pratipaśyeyur vaśitvaṃ yadi vai bhavet
english: If sovereign mastery were truly within reach, none would die, none would grow old, all would fulfill every desire, and none would ever face what is unwished.

sanskrit: upary upari lokasya sarvo gantuṃ samīhate yatate ca yathāśakti na ca tad vartate tathā
english: Everyone strives to rise higher and higher in the world and exerts himself according to his capacity — yet things do not turn out that way.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ saṃpradṛśyante tulyanakṣatramaṅgalāḥ mahac ca phalavaiṣamyaṃ dṛśyate karmasaṃdhiṣu
english: Many are seen who share the same birth-star and auspicious signs, yet great inequality of result is observed at the junctures of their actions.

sanskrit: na kaś cid īśate brahman svayaṃgrāhasya sattama karmaṇāṃ prākṛtānāṃ vai iha siddhiḥ pradṛśyate
english: No one is master of seizing things by his own will alone, O brahmin, O best of good men — the fulfillment of ordinary actions is seen to depend on something else.

sanskrit: yathā śrutir iyaṃ brahman jīvaḥ kila sanātanaḥ śarīram adhruvaṃ loke sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām iha
english: As this scriptural teaching holds, O brahmin: the self is indeed eternal, while the body in this world is impermanent for all living beings.

sanskrit: vadhyamāne śarīre tu dehanāśo bhavaty uta jīvaḥ saṃkramate 'nyatra karmabandhanibandhanaḥ
english: When the body is destroyed, the body perishes indeed; but the self migrates elsewhere, bound by the bonds of its accumulated karma.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca kathaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha jīvo bhavati śāśvataḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ jñātuṃ tattvena vadatāṃ vara
english: The brahmin said: How is the self eternal, O best among upholders of dharma? I wish to know this truth — tell me, O best among those who speak truthfully.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca na jīvanāśo 'sti hi dehabhede; mithyaitad āhur mriyateti mūḍhāḥ jīvas tu dehāntaritaḥ prayāti; daśārdhataivāsya śarīrabhedaḥ
english: The hunter said: There is no destruction of the self when the body dissolves; the fools who say 'it dies' speak falsely. The self departs, having passed through the body; the dissolution of the body is as nothing compared to the self.

sanskrit: anyo hi nāśnāti kṛtaṃ hi karma; sa eva kartā sukhaduḥkhabhāgī yat tena kiṃ cid dhi kṛtaṃ hi karma; tad aśnute nāsti kṛtasya nāśaḥ
english: For another does not eat the fruit of an action that has been done; the very doer himself experiences pleasure and pain. Whatever action has been done by him, he reaps that — there is no destruction of what has been done.

sanskrit: apuṇyaśīlāś ca bhavanti puṇyā; narottamāḥ pāpakṛto bhavanti naro 'nuyātas tv iha karmabhiḥ svais; tataḥ samutpadyati bhāvitas taiḥ
english: Those of sinful disposition may become meritorious, and best among men may become sinners — a man here is accompanied by his own actions, and is reborn shaped by them.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca kathaṃ saṃbhavate yonau kathaṃ vā puṇyapāpayoḥ jātīḥ puṇyā hy apuṇyāś ca kathaṃ gacchati sattama
english: The brahmin said: How does conception in the womb occur? How do merit and demerit operate? How does one go to auspicious or inauspicious births, O good one?

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca garbhādhānasamāyuktaṃ karmedaṃ saṃpradṛśyate samāsena tu te kṣipraṃ pravakṣyāmi dvijottama
english: The hunter said: This action connected with the planting of the embryo is observed here — I will explain it to you briefly and quickly, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: yathā saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ punar eva prajāyate śubhakṛc chubhayonīṣu pāpakṛt pāpayoniṣu
english: Just as one who has accumulated provisions is born again, the doer of good is born in auspicious wombs, and the doer of evil in evil wombs.

sanskrit: śubhaiḥ prayogair devatvaṃ vyāmiśrair mānuṣo bhavet mohanīyair viyonīṣu tv adhogāmī ca kilbiṣaiḥ
english: By auspicious conduct one attains divinity; by mixed actions one becomes human; by deluding means one goes to lower births; and by sinful deeds one descends further.

sanskrit: jātimṛtyujarāduḥkhaiḥ satataṃ samabhidrutaḥ saṃsāre pacyamānaś ca doṣair ātmakṛtair naraḥ
english: Constantly assailed by the sufferings of birth, death, and old age, and cooked in the cycle of existence by the faults he himself has made, man wanders on.

sanskrit: tiryagyonisahasrāṇi gatvā narakam eva ca jīvāḥ saṃparivartante karmabandhanibandhanāḥ
english: Having passed through thousands of animal births and through hell itself, souls revolve in this cycle, bound by the bonds of karma.

sanskrit: jantus tu karmabhis tais taiḥ svakṛtaiḥ pretya duḥkhitaḥ tadduḥkhapratighātārtham apuṇyāṃ yonim aśnute
english: The creature, suffering after death on account of its own various actions, obtains a low birth for the purpose of counteracting that suffering.

sanskrit: tataḥ karma samādatte punar anyan navaṃ bahu pacyate tu punas tena bhuktvāpathyam ivāturaḥ
english: Then again it undertakes new and manifold actions, and is cooked anew by them — just as a sick man who eats harmful food suffers again.

sanskrit: ajasram eva duḥkhārto 'duḥkhitaḥ sukhasaṃjñitaḥ tato 'nivṛttabandhatvāt karmaṇām udayād api parikrāmati saṃsāre cakravad bahuvedanaḥ
english: Perpetually tormented yet calling itself free from pain and naming its state 'happiness,' and because its bondage never ceases even with the rise of new actions, it wanders through samsara like a wheel, experiencing many sufferings.

sanskrit: sa cen nivṛttabandhas tu viśuddhaś cāpi karmabhiḥ prāpnoti sukṛtāṃl lokān yatra gatvā na śocati
english: But if one has dissolved its bonds and is purified in its actions, it attains the worlds of the meritorious — having gone there, it grieves no more.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kurvan pāpavṛttaḥ pāpasyāntaṃ na gacchati tasmāt puṇyaṃ yatet kartuṃ varjayeta ca pātakam
english: One who commits evil and lives evilly never reaches the end of sin; therefore one should strive to perform meritorious deeds and shun transgression.

sanskrit: anasūyuḥ kṛtajñaś ca kalyāṇāny eva sevate sukhāni dharmam arthaṃ ca svargaṃ ca labhate naraḥ
english: One who is free from envy and grateful cultivates only the auspicious; such a man attains happiness, dharma, wealth, and heaven.

sanskrit: saṃskṛtasya hi dāntasya niyatasya yatātmanaḥ prājñasyānantarā vṛttir iha loke paratra ca
english: For the man of culture, self-controlled, disciplined, with mastered soul and wise — his sustenance is unobstructed, both in this world and the next.

sanskrit: satāṃ dharmeṇa varteta kriyāṃ śiṣṭavad ācaret asaṃkleśena lokasya vṛttiṃ lipseta vai dvija
english: One should live by the dharma of the good, conduct one's actions as the learned do, and seek one's livelihood without causing distress to the world, O twice-born.

sanskrit: santi hy āgatavijñānāḥ śiṣṭāḥ śāstravicakṣaṇāḥ svadharmeṇa kriyā loke karmaṇaḥ so 'py asaṃkaraḥ
english: For there are learned men, well-versed in scripture, who have attained wisdom; by living according to one's own dharma, action in the world remains without confusion.

sanskrit: prājño dharmeṇa ramate dharmaṃ caivopajīvati tasya dharmād avāpteṣu dhaneṣu dvijasattama tasyaiva siñcate mūlaṃ guṇān paśyati yatra vai
english: The wise man delights in dharma and lives by dharma; with the wealth obtained through dharma, O best of twice-born, he waters its very root and perceives the virtues therein.

sanskrit: dharmātmā bhavati hy evaṃ cittaṃ cāsya prasīdati sa maitrajanasaṃtuṣṭa iha pretya ca nandati
english: In this way he becomes righteous of soul and his mind grows serene; content among kindly people, he rejoices both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: śabdaṃ sparśaṃ tathā rūpaṃ gandhān iṣṭāṃś ca sattama prabhutvaṃ labhate cāpi dharmasyaitat phalaṃ viduḥ
english: Sound, touch, form, desired fragrances, and lordly power — all these he obtains; the wise know this to be the fruit of dharma, O good man.

sanskrit: dharmasya ca phalaṃ labdhvā na tṛpyati mahādvija atṛpyamāṇo nirvedam ādatte jñānacakṣuṣā
english: Having obtained the fruit of dharma, he is not satisfied, O great twice-born; and in that dissatisfaction he takes up dispassion with the eye of knowledge.

sanskrit: prajñācakṣur nara iha doṣaṃ naivānurudhyate virajyati yathākāmaṃ na ca dharmaṃ vimuñcati
english: The man whose eye is wisdom does not here conform to any fault; he becomes dispassionate as he wishes, yet does not abandon dharma.

sanskrit: sarvatyāge ca yatate dṛṣṭvā lokaṃ kṣayātmakam tato mokṣe prayatate nānupāyād upāyataḥ
english: Having seen the world to be of a perishing nature, he strives toward the renunciation of all things; then he strives toward liberation — not by indirect means but by the direct path.

sanskrit: evaṃ nirvedam ādatte pāpaṃ karma jahāti ca dhārmikaś cāpi bhavati mokṣaṃ ca labhate param
english: Thus he takes up dispassion, abandons sinful action, becomes righteous, and attains supreme liberation.

sanskrit: tapo niḥśreyasaṃ jantos tasya mūlaṃ śamo damaḥ tena sarvān avāpnoti kāmān yān manasecchati
english: Austerity is the highest good for a living being; its root is tranquility and self-restraint. By that one attains all the desires that the mind wishes for.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ nirodhena satyena ca damena ca brahmaṇaḥ padam āpnoti yat paraṃ dvijasattama
english: By the restraint of the senses, by truth, and by self-control, one attains the supreme state of Brahman, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca indriyāṇi tu yāny āhuḥ kāni tāni yatavrata nigrahaś ca kathaṃ kāryo nigrahasya ca kiṃ phalam
english: The brahmin said: What are those that are called the senses, O you of firm vows? How is their restraint to be practiced, and what is the fruit of that restraint?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca phalam āpnoti teṣāṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara etad icchāmi tattvena dharmaṃ jñātuṃ sudhārmika
english: And how does one attain the fruit thereof, O best among upholders of dharma? I desire to know this dharma in truth, O you who are deeply righteous.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktas tu vipreṇa dharmavyādho yudhiṣṭhira pratyuvāca yathā vipraṃ tac chṛṇuṣva narādhipa
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thus addressed by the brahmin, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the dharma-hunter replied to the brahmin accordingly — hear that, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca vijñānārthaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ manaḥ pūrvaṃ pravartate tat prāpya kāmaṃ bhajate krodhaṃ ca dvijasattama
english: The hunter said: For the purpose of knowing, the mind of human beings first sets itself in motion; having obtained its object, it then indulges in desire and anger, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: tatas tadarthaṃ yatate karma cārabhate mahat iṣṭānāṃ rūpagandhānām abhyāsaṃ ca niṣevate
english: Then for that very purpose it strives and undertakes great action; it constantly pursues the habituation of desired forms and fragrances.

sanskrit: tato rāgaḥ prabhavati dveṣaś ca tadanantaram tato lobhaḥ prabhavati mohaś ca tadanantaram
english: From that arises passion, and immediately after it hatred; from that arises greed, and immediately after it delusion.

sanskrit: tasya lobhābhibhūtasya rāgadveṣahatasya ca na dharme jāyate buddhir vyājād dharmaṃ karoti ca
english: Of one overwhelmed by greed and struck down by passion and hatred, the intellect does not arise toward dharma; he performs dharma only through pretense.

sanskrit: vyājena carate dharmam arthaṃ vyājena rocate vyājena sidhyamāneṣu dhaneṣu dvijasattama tatraiva ramate buddhis tataḥ pāpaṃ cikīrṣati
english: He practices dharma by pretense, he takes pleasure in wealth by pretense; when wealth is acquired through pretense, O best of twice-born, the intellect delights in that very thing and then desires to commit sin.

sanskrit: suhṛdbhir vāryamāṇaś ca paṇḍitaiś ca dvijottama uttaraṃ śrutisaṃbaddhaṃ bravīti śrutiyojitam
english: Even when restrained by friends and by learned men, O best of twice-born, he speaks a reply connected to scripture, invoking scripture to justify himself.

sanskrit: adharmas trividhas tasya vardhate rāgadoṣataḥ pāpaṃ cintayate cāpi bravīti ca karoti ca
english: Adharma in three forms grows in him out of the fault of passion: he thinks sin, speaks sin, and commits sin.

sanskrit: tasyādharmapravṛttasya guṇā naśyanti sādhavaḥ ekaśīlāś ca mitratvaṃ bhajante pāpakarmiṇaḥ
english: For one who has turned toward adharma, good virtues perish; and those who are of like character come to enjoy his friendship — those who commit evil actions.

sanskrit: sa tenāsukham āpnoti paratra ca vihanyate pāpātmā bhavati hy evaṃ dharmalābhaṃ tu me śṛṇu
english: By this he obtains misery and is struck down in the hereafter — thus one becomes of sinful soul. Now hear from me the gaining of dharma.

sanskrit: yas tv etān prajñayā doṣān pūrvam evānupaśyati kuśalaḥ sukhaduḥkheṣu sādhūṃś cāpy upasevate tasya sādhusamārambhād buddhir dharmeṣu jāyate
english: But he who by wisdom foresees these very faults from the outset, who is skilled in pleasure and pain and frequents the company of the virtuous — through association with good beginnings, his intellect is born toward the ways of dharma.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca bravīṣi sūnṛtaṃ dharmaṃ yasya vaktā na vidyate divyaprabhāvaḥ sumahān ṛṣir eva mato 'si me
english: The brahmin said: You speak dharma that is true and pleasant — there is no other speaker of it like you. Of divine splendor and exceeding greatness, you seem to me truly a sage.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca brāhmaṇā vai mahābhāgāḥ pitaro 'grabhujaḥ sadā teṣāṃ sarvātmanā kāryaṃ priyaṃ loke manīṣiṇā
english: The hunter said: Brahmins are indeed the most fortunate; they are the forefathers who partake first always. A wise man should with all his soul do what pleases them in the world.

sanskrit: yat teṣāṃ ca priyaṃ tat te vakṣyāmi dvijasattama namaskṛtvā brāhmaṇebhyo brāhmīṃ vidyāṃ nibodha me
english: What pleases them I will tell you, O best of twice-born — having paid homage to the brahmins, learn from me the knowledge born of Brahman.

sanskrit: idaṃ viśvaṃ jagat sarvam ajayyaṃ cāpi sarvaśaḥ mahābhūtātmakaṃ brahman nātaḥ parataraṃ bhavet
english: This entire universe, wholly unconquerable in every respect, O brahmin, has the great elements as its soul; there is nothing higher than this.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni khaṃ vāyur agnir āpas tathā ca bhūḥ śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca tadguṇāḥ
english: The great elements are: space, wind, fire, water, and earth — and sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are their qualities.

sanskrit: teṣām api guṇāḥ sarve guṇavṛttiḥ parasparam pūrvapūrvaguṇāḥ sarve kramaśo guṇiṣu triṣu
english: All of their qualities operate mutually on one another; each carries forward the qualities of the one preceding it — all in succession among the three modes of being.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhas tu cetanā nāma mana ity abhidhīyate saptamī tu bhaved buddhir ahaṃkāras tataḥ param
english: The sixth is named consciousness — it is called the mind; the seventh is the intellect; and after that comes the ego-sense.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi ca pañcaiva rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamas tathā ity eṣa saptadaśako rāśir avyaktasaṃjñakaḥ
english: And the five senses, along with rajas, sattva, and tamas — this is the group of seventeen known by the name of the unmanifest.

sanskrit: sarvair ihendriyārthais tu vyaktāvyaktaiḥ susaṃvṛtaḥ caturviṃśaka ity eṣa vyaktāvyaktamayo guṇaḥ etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ kiṃ bhūyo śrotum icchasi
english: Perfectly enveloped by all the objects of the senses here, both manifest and unmanifest, this is the twenty-fourth — the principle composed of both manifest and unmanifest. All this has been declared to you; what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktaḥ sa vipras tu dharmavyādhena bhārata kathām akathayad bhūyo manasaḥ prītivardhanīm
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thus addressed by the dharma-hunter, O Bhārata, that brahmin then spoke once more a discourse that increases the joy of the mind.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa mahābhūtāni yāny āhuḥ pañca dharmavidāṃ vara ekaikasya guṇān samyak pañcānām api me vada
english: The brahmin said: O best among those who know dharma, those five great elements of which they speak — tell me properly the qualities of each of the five individually.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca bhūmir āpas tathā jyotir vāyur ākāśam eva ca guṇottarāṇi sarvāṇi teṣāṃ vakṣyāmi te guṇān
english: The hunter said: Earth, water, fire, wind, and space — all have qualities exceeding one another; I will tell you their qualities.

sanskrit: bhūmiḥ pañcaguṇā brahmann udakaṃ ca caturguṇam guṇās trayas tejasi ca trayaś cākāśavātayoḥ
english: Earth has five qualities, O brahmin, and water has four; fire has three qualities, and space and wind each have two — or rather three between them.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ ete guṇāḥ pañca bhūmeḥ sarvebhyo guṇavattarāḥ
english: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth — these five qualities of earth are richest in qualities compared to all others.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca rasaś cāpi dvijottama apām ete guṇā brahman kīrtitās tava suvrata
english: Sound, touch, form, and taste — O best of twice-born, O brahmin, O you of excellent vows, these are proclaimed to be the qualities of water.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca tejaso 'tha guṇās trayaḥ śabdaḥ sparśaś ca vāyau tu śabda ākāśa eva ca
english: Sound, touch, and form — these three are the qualities of fire. In wind there are sound and touch; in space, sound alone.

sanskrit: ete pañcadaśa brahman guṇā bhūteṣu pañcasu vartante sarvabhūteṣu yeṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ anyonyaṃ nātivartante saṃpac ca bhavati dvija
english: These fifteen qualities, O brahmin, abide in the five elements — they are present in all beings, in whom the worlds are grounded. They do not transgress one another, and their conjunction brings well-being, O twice-born.

sanskrit: yadā tu viṣamībhāvam ācaranti carācarāḥ tadā dehī deham anyaṃ vyatirohati kālataḥ
english: But when the moving and unmoving beings enter into a state of imbalance, then the embodied soul in the course of time mounts another body.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyā vinaśyanti jāyante cānupūrvaśaḥ tatra tatra hi dṛśyante dhātavaḥ pāñcabhautikāḥ yair āvṛtam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: In succession they perish, and in succession they are born; here and there the elements composed of the five great ones are seen — by which this entire world, of moving and unmoving things, is enveloped.
